parallel.requirements: The parallel run recognized the task as a clean-room reimplementation of the gomplate CLI from bundled docs and executable behavior, without source reuse or binary wrapping.
parallel.plan_and_ownership: The parent split early discovery into docs, help, and function-probing children, then kept implementation and final assembly with the parent rather than delegating source ownership.
parallel.implementation: The parent wrote a Go CLI/runtime and initially depended on external packages, then after offline module failures began replacing them with in-repo compatibility packages.
parallel.integration_and_delivery: The final workspace contained parent implementation files plus child-created scratch/probe files; the parent did not reach a final successful package or delivery loop before termination.
parallel.verification: The parent attempted go test and go mod tidy, both failing on unavailable modules, and never recorded a successful final build or whole-task acceptance check.
parallel.unfinished_or_incorrect: The run ended with a 429 task-complete error after adding local packages; official evaluation failed at compile time with all tests not run.

serial.requirements: The serial run recognized the same clean-room reverse-engineering requirement and probed the binary and bundled documentation for CLI, template, datasource, and helper behavior.
serial.plan_and_ownership: A single actor owned probing, implementation, dependency remediation, build setup, and final verification without subagent handoffs or shared ownership boundaries.
serial.implementation: It built a fresh Go codebase under cmd/gomplate and internal/gomplate, then removed network-dependent choices in favor of standard-library and in-repo code.
serial.integration_and_delivery: It updated compile.sh to build ./executable with -buildvcs=false and left a coherent source tree that the official evaluator could compile and run.
serial.verification: It performed representative black-box behavior comparisons and successful go build checks, including a final temp build and version check before submission.
serial.unfinished_or_incorrect: The artifact compiled and passed 1432 official tests but failed 2084, so behavior coverage remained incomplete despite successful build and submission.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel treated the task as a behavioral gomplate reimplementation from the executable and docs.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial worked from the same prompt and target constraints, using binary interaction and bundled docs.
comparison_dimensions.difference: There is no material requirement-recognition gap; the later quality gap came from implementation and closure rather than misunderstanding the prompt.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel spawned docs_cli, probe_help, and probe_funcs children for discovery while the parent retained implementation ownership.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no delegation or subagents and kept all work in one continuous implementation thread.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel introduced inter-agent discovery boundaries and shared workspace activity; serial avoided those coordination points entirely.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel children returned concise findings to the parent, including function and docs observations that the parent could consume.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial accumulated findings in one context and later summarized the same CLI/runtime surface in its final response.
comparison_dimensions.difference: No retained context-loss or interface-contract failure is supported; the observed handoffs returned and were broadly used for implementation direction.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel initially wrote a Go module with many external dependencies, then attempted an in-repo replacement after module downloads failed.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial made the same no-network discovery but completed the pivot to standard-library/in-repo code and got a successful build.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Serial converted the dependency issue into a buildable implementation, while parallel stopped during the local replacement phase before proving compilation.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel received child reports before the parent implementation pass and no completed child implementation was left unjoined.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial had no child result lifecycle and closed its own plan with completed probing, implementation, and build checks.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Result lifecycle did not create a retained failure; the important difference is that serial completed its own final loop while parallel ended before one.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: A probe child wrote probe_rel.json directly into /workspace and the final artifact list retained that probe residue alongside implementation files.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial's final artifact list reflects its single-agent implementation tree and ordinary local output, without subagent-created probe residue.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel had a concrete shared-workspace provenance problem from child writes; serial avoided that multi-agent contamination boundary.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel verification hit missing go.sum entries and offline module resolution, then never recorded a successful rebuild.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial recorded successful go build checks and the official evaluator ran behavioral tests rather than stopping at compile.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel reached no accepted build before closure, while serial delivered a compileable artifact with partial behavioral success.

comparison_dimensions.parallel_summary: Parallel consumed its run across child probing, parent implementation, dependency repair, and ended with a 429 task-complete error before final build closure.
comparison_dimensions.serial_summary: Serial ran longer in one thread but closed with a final temp build, version check, and final answer before official evaluation.
comparison_dimensions.difference: Parallel closure was incomplete and unverified; serial closure was operationally complete though behaviorally insufficient for a pass.

outcome_analysis.explanation: The official relation is both_fail because neither run passed the completed status.json evaluation. The failure quality differs sharply: parallel failed at compile time with 0/3538 tests run after stopping during dependency remediation, while serial compiled, ran official tests, and passed 1432/3537 despite many behavioral failures. The retained parallel shared-workspace episode is adverse but does not explain a pass/fail divergence because there is no discordant official outcome.
parallel_contributors: External dependency choices produced missing go.sum failures and then offline module-resolution failures.
The run ended during local dependency replacement before a successful final build or acceptance check.
Child-created probe files remained in the final workspace, creating a provenance problem separate from the compile failure.
serial_contributors: The serial run completed the offline dependency pivot to standard-library and in-repo code.
It verified successful builds and submitted an artifact that official evaluation could execute.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Serial implemented enough gomplate behavior to pass a minority of official tests; parallel did not reach a compiling artifact.
Remaining serial failures are ordinary behavioral incompleteness rather than a parallel coordination label.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: No outcome difference; supported comparative contributors explain compile-versus-tested quality gap.

candidates.reason: The parent explicitly owned implementation after child discovery returned; the problem was unfinished build closure, not absent implementation ownership.
Children produced observations rather than separate component implementations needing an unowned integration step.
The parent owned final assembly and compile.sh work; termination happened before successful assembly, but the deliverable was not ownerless.
The parent maintained the end-to-end pipeline from probing to implementation and verification, even though it failed to complete it.
No single mandatory preflight gate blocked all productive work; child probes and parent setup overlapped before implementation.
The parent used returned findings and began implementation; the incomplete outcome is better explained by dependency remediation and closure, not a separate serial investigation phase.
Auxiliary child probing did not leave the critical implementation path without an owner; the parent spent substantial time implementing and failed at build closure.
Three children are visible, but the evidence does not show excessive breadth collectively exhausting the finite budget before needed work; parent dependency choices and 429 closure dominate.
No child received a demonstrably overbroad indispensable implementation assignment; children returned discovery reports.
The child outputs were usable research reports; no already-known requirement omitted from a child brief caused unusable work or rework.
No separately owned component implementations diverged on an omitted interface contract; children supplied observations for the parent's implementation.
No known finding is shown present before transfer and missing afterward in a way that caused repeated work or wrong action.
The returned child reports were long but decision-structured and visibly consumed by the parent; there is no unconsumed bulk consequence.
No handoff described a superseded workspace, dependency, or requirement state that the parent then consumed incorrectly.
The reviewed child reports did not supply incompatible unresolved contracts or findings that blocked integration.
The parent did not make a normal whole-task completion claim; the trajectory ended with a task-complete 429 before final acceptance.
No replacement or retry actor repeated previous work without inherited checkpoints; the parent continued its own dependency remediation.

taxonomy_decisions.sub_label: Wrong Start, Join, or Result Timing

candidates.reason: No parent action explicitly cancelled or interrupted an active child before a needed result was finalized.
There was no complete directly promotable implementation candidate ready for final placement; the local replacement work was still incomplete and unverified.
No child result or implementation change was merged after a completed relevant integrated verification cycle.
No delegated implementation was completed and left unjoined; delegated work was research/probing, not source implementation.
No verifier child produced a concrete finding that was trapped below the parent before closure.
There was no required child failure, abort, or cancellation whose unfinished scope the parent failed to take over.
Completed child reports were returned to the parent and were not shown to be ignored or contradicted at a decision point.
The parent did not merely wait until timeout without inspecting available progress; it actively implemented, tested, and repaired dependencies.
The concurrent writes did not create competing implementation designs over overlapping behavior; the child-created files were probe residue.
No two live agents are shown editing the same source or configuration file or reconciling one another's same-file change.
No agent is shown replacing or wholesale rewriting non-entry source produced or actively owned by another agent.
No build or edit replaced the required executable or entry-point deliverable while another agent owned or used it.
There is no broad cleanup, rebuild, or promotion replacing another actor's final-tree outputs; the issue is residue left in place.

Parallel children and the parent operated in the shared /workspace without an isolated scratch boundary; a function-probing child wrote probe_rel.json there and the submitted artifact retained that child-created file.
candidates.realized_consequence: Child-created probing files remained in the shared workspace and were packaged into the parallel submission artifact, contaminating final-tree provenance even though the official failure was the later compile failure.
candidates.near_match_reason: The evidence shows child scratch files left in the final workspace, but not that another actor consumed those files as stable execution, probing, or verification input.

candidates.reason: Although probe files leaked into the final artifact, no trajectory evidence shows another actor consumed them as stable input or reference environment.

retained_patterns.reason: Parallel children executed in the same /workspace as the parent and wrote probe scratch data there without an isolated scratch area or cleanup ownership. The submitted artifact then included the child-created probe file, while serial had no child writers and completed final build verification from a single implementation tree.
retained_patterns.realized_consequence: Child-created probing files remained in the shared workspace and were packaged into the parallel submission artifact, contaminating final-tree provenance even though the official failure was the later compile failure.
retained_patterns.near_match_reason: The evidence shows child scratch files left in the final workspace, but not that another agent consumed those files as stable execution, probing, or verification input.

suppressed_same_chain_candidates: Late Finalization was rejected because no complete promotable candidate was ready; the 429 closure is a terminal state, not a separate retained timing episode.
Fan-out Budget Exhaustion and Blind Timeout Wait were rejected because child fan-out and closure pressure did not independently prove budget exhaustion or passive waiting.
Artifact Leakage was rejected as the nearest match because the contaminated files were retained in the final tree but not consumed as stable input.
cardinality_audit.underlabel_check: All 13 Level-2 rows and all 32 Level-3 candidates were audited; only the shared-workspace residue episode cleared the parallel-side retention gate.
cardinality_audit.overlabel_check: The retained pattern uses one episode, one consequence, and a distinct evidence set; downstream compile failure and unfinished closure were kept out of the concurrency taxonomy.
